name: Vetch
role: Section Officer — the party's immediate superior
designNotes:
Created at Ingram's suggestion: 'we need to put someone in charge of the PC group, someone who isn't a great or nice person, an antagonist from within the system who the players will eventually defeat by proving them wrong, out performing their expectations and eventually they'll be promoted out of that petty tyrants clutches.'

Full arc, the five stages, the transmission-chain reading and his voice samples: quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/the-section-officer.md. Do not author a defeat schedule -- the stage table there is the shape of where this goes, not a timetable, and he stays an unsolved problem for the start of the adventure while also being the party's main point of contact with the Directorate.

Named Vetch, surname only, by Ingram on 2026-09-21 (open-questions.json#section-officer-name): a name that sounds like a middling rank on a duty roster rather than a villain.

facts.text: He has done every job he hands out, properly, and he knows what a bad one looks like. Talk to him about the work and you get a different man than the one who talks about you.

revealTrigger.narrative: Watching him inspect the sea wall -- he tests a surface with a thumbnail rather than looking at it, and everything he asks about is real.

facts.text: He cannot let a wrong statement stand in front of him. Say something incorrect about a procedure and he will correct it, in full, whether or not he meant to tell you.
Somebody well above him has taken an interest in his section and he does not know who. He is frightened of exactly the thing the party is curious about.

revealTrigger.narrative: Reading the memorandum in his out-tray, or getting the countersignature off the roster and asking him about it.

facts.text: His own paperwork is flawless, always, because it is the one thing nobody can take off him. An appeal made correctly in writing gets further with him than any appeal made out loud.

He cannot be visibly surprised. Do something he did not expect and he pauses for one beat and then explains that it was the intention. A player who spots the pattern can use it: get him to claim a plan in front of somebody, and he is committed to it, because taking it back would mean admitting he was surprised.

revealTrigger.narrative: Succeeding at something he plainly did not expect, twice, and paying attention to how he receives it both times.

facts.text: He went through this himself as a new intake and came out believing the system works. Raised directly, it is the one subject on which he stops being procedural for a moment. He does not soften afterwards and he will not discuss it twice.

revealTrigger.narrative: Somebody who was serving then mentions it, or he says it himself at the end of a very long day and immediately moves on.
